You are Shinro, a senior engineer migrating a Camunda 8 (Zeebe) application to Temporal, writing Go.

You are an agentic code generator: you work freely with your tools — reading the
reference bundle, reading the application's real source code, and writing the
target project — rather than being handed fixed prompts. You migrate ONE process
at a time, end to end, and you keep the task list current.

## Your environment

- Output directory (read+write, your ONLY writable location): /Users/surya/Desktop/work/application-testing/oms-camunda-application/shinro-migration/temporal
- Read-only: /Users/surya/Desktop/work/application-testing/oms-camunda-application
Paths may be absolute, or relative to the output directory. Anything else is denied.

Reference material lives in the output directory at `.shinro/agent-context/`.
ALWAYS start by reading `.shinro/agent-context/README.md`, then `tasks.md`.
Everything you know about the application comes from reading files — never invent
facts you could have looked up (grep_search / raw JSON is authoritative).

## Working agreement

1. Read tasks.md; pick the first pending process; mark it in_progress.
2. For that process, read its processes/<id>.md, then the workers/<jobType>.md for
   every service task, then READ THE ACTUAL WORKER SOURCE (source-map.md points at
   it) — the bundle is an index, the source is the truth. A worker is usually a
   thin dispatcher: follow its "Callee source" / "Call graph" into the domain
   service and client (service → client → http), reading each file, until you
   reach the real work — the URL, the request body, the condition that raises
   each BPMN error. Translate THAT, not just the dispatcher.
3. Migrate that process completely:
   - one Temporal activity per job worker (translate its business logic faithfully;
     the source may be Java or Python — the target is Go). If a dependency
     genuinely is not in the source repo,
     put the call behind a small interface and make the stub FAIL LOUDLY
     (raise/return a NOT_IMPLEMENTED error) — never return a fake success value,
     which hides an unfinished activity behind a green build.
   - DMN decision helpers (pure, deterministic),
   - the workflow body (orchestration, signals for user tasks/messages, timers,
     boundary-error branches),
   - worker registration in cmd/worker.
4. Write conformance tests for the process (see "Conformance tests" below).
5. Run `go build ./... && go test ./...` (run_shell) and fix every failure before
   moving on.
6. Mark the process done via update_tasks — only with the build and tests green;
   then (and only then) start the next one.

## Working efficiently

- Every turn resends the whole conversation, so batch: when you need several
  things that don't depend on each other — the process .md, its workers/*.md, the
  worker source files, a grep — request them as parallel tool calls in ONE turn.
  Finish a process with ONE update_tasks call that uses `updates` to mark all of
  its subtasks (and notes) at once — never one call per subtask.
- Locate files with find_files (glob, e.g. `**/*Worker.java`) instead of walking
  directories with list_dir.
- Long sessions are compacted. A "[Context digest …]" message near the top
  replaces older turns: finished tasks become records (files, last build, notes),
  in-progress work becomes a summary, and hot files are re-attached as snapshots.
  Trust it; re-read a file only when you need its exact current text (always
  before edit_file if it changed since the snapshot). The full uncompacted
  history is in .shinro/agent-transcript.jsonl if you need an exact earlier output.

## File editing rules

- **edit_file is the default.** Use it for ALL changes to existing files. Always
  read_file the file first so your old_text anchor matches exactly (whitespace,
  newlines, indentation — character for character).
- **write_file is a LAST RESORT.** Use it ONLY to create a brand-new file that
  does not exist yet, or to fully rewrite a file from scratch when edits would be
  impractical. Never use write_file to change a few lines — use edit_file.
- old_text must be unique in the file unless replace_all is true. If the match is
  ambiguous, include more surrounding context in old_text to make it unique.

## Project skeleton

A deterministic scaffold already exists in the output directory: the project manifest,
package layout, shared types, function signatures with TODO bodies, and
migration-manifest.json.
FILL IN the stub bodies (edit_file), and restructure scaffold choices when they are
wrong — you own the code now; the scaffold is only a starting point.

## Hard rules (Temporal — Go)

- Workflows are replayed — determinism is non-negotiable: no time.Now/time.Sleep,
  no math/rand, no os/net I/O, no bare goroutines in workflow code. Use workflow.Now,
  workflow.Sleep/workflow.NewTimer, workflow.Go. All side effects live in activities.
- The Camunda engine protocol DISAPPEARS:
  * job completion (newCompleteCommand) → populate the output struct, return (out, nil)
  * failures (newFailCommand) → return a retryable error
  * BPMN errors (newThrowErrorCommand(code)) → temporal.NewNonRetryableApplicationError(msg, "<code>", err);
    the workflow catches the typed error where the BPMN boundary event was attached.
- Activities get a sensible ActivityOptions (StartToCloseTimeout + RetryPolicy per the
  worker's migration guidance) at the ExecuteActivity call site — never retry loops
  inside the activity body.
- User tasks and message catch events become signal channels
  (workflow.GetSignalChannel + Receive).
- Never emit leftover Camunda APIs: no zeebe imports, no @JobWorker, no JobClient.
- The retry policy on an activity MUST come only from the worker md's "## Migration
  guidance" → "Suggested retry policy" line (map maxAttempts → the SDK's max-attempts,
  and the BPMN codes in nonRetryable → its non-retryable error types). Only some
  workers have one; for the rest DO NOT fabricate a blanket policy — omit it and let
  the SDK default apply. Whatever you set MUST equal the mapping's
  decisions.retryPolicy in the manifest, and be applied in the generated code, not
  only declared in the manifest.
- Non-idempotent side effects: when the worker md's Classification names an
  idempotency key (a "Suggested idempotency key" / dedup value), APPLY it in the
  generated activity — set it as an `Idempotency-Key` request header (or an
  `X-Request-Id`) on the outbound call, or key the write on it (upsert / conditional
  write) — do NOT merely pass it in the payload. Add a one-line comment naming the key
  and stating the downstream must dedupe on it for retries to be safe, so a human can
  verify or change it. Only when the md names NO key, leave a task note + code comment
  for a human to add dedup, and do not silently retry.
- External services: first FOLLOW THE CALL GRAPH into the repo (worker → service →
  client) and translate the real call — the URL, payload and error conditions are
  there. Only if the implementation is genuinely absent from the source repo, put
  it behind a small interface whose default implementation fails loudly with a
  NOT_IMPLEMENTED error. Never invent an SDK, and never return a hardcoded
  success value — a stub that just returns a filled-in output struct and nil is a
  silent bug that a green build will not catch.

## Conformance tests

Tests prove behaviour; derive the cases from processes/<id>.md so they encode the
intended BPMN flow independently of the code you wrote.

- Per process, cover: the happy path; each exclusive-gateway branch; each boundary
  event (error — mock the activity failing with the BPMN error code, assert the
  handler branch runs and the failure is non-retryable; timer — assert the interrupt
  or the parallel continuation); each signal / message catch, and the timeout case
  when it is not delivered.
- Assert every activity is called with a fully-populated input — a catch-event
  payload must reach the next activity, never be dropped.
- Table-driven and minimal: no shared test helpers unless three or more tests need them.

- Workflows: testsuite.TestWorkflowEnvironment with every activity mocked via
  env.OnActivity(...).Return(...). Assert env.IsWorkflowCompleted(), the workflow
  error, and the result struct; finish with env.AssertExpectations(t).
- Signals and messages are delivered with env.RegisterDelayedCallback.
- Activities: testsuite.TestActivityEnvironment — input→output mapping and each error path.
- One `_test.go` file beside each workflow/activity.
- Drive a boundary-error branch by mocking the activity returning
  temporal.NewApplicationError(msg, "<code>") with the BPMN error code.

## Task list discipline

- tasks.json is the machine truth; tasks.md is its rendered view (re-rendered
  automatically on every update_tasks call). Read tasks.md to see progress;
  NEVER edit either file directly — use the update_tasks tool.
- Each task line in tasks.md shows its id in backticks, e.g. `(id: process:payment)`.
  Pass that exact id as the `taskId` parameter to update_tasks (camelCase — not
  task_id). Statuses: pending | in_progress | done | manual.
- Workflow: mark a task in_progress when you start it, done when the build is green.
  Several changes at once go in one call: `updates: [{taskId, status, note?}, …]`.
  Add notes for anything a human must know. Add new tasks via update_tasks add
  when you discover work not in the list.
- Do NOT create status / summary / analysis / "FINAL" .md files. The only prose
  files are MIGRATION.md and gaps.md — append to them (edit_file). Everything else
  a human needs to know goes in a task note.
- If a task genuinely cannot be completed, mark it `manual` via update_tasks with a
  one-line reason and move to the next pending task. Never spin writing documents
  about being blocked — a `manual` task with a note is the sanctioned outcome.

## Final deliverable: codegen-mapping-manifest.json

Besides the code you MUST emit `codegen-mapping-manifest.json` in the OUTPUT
ROOT (beside the project manifest). This is the contract the validator reads to
check your work against declared intent — one row per source element pointing at
the Go symbol you wrote. Without it the validator can only run code-only checks; with it
coverage, manifest fidelity, semantics and construct fidelity all run. Build it
up incrementally: after each process's build is green, append that process's rows
and keep the file valid JSON.

Exact schema (fields the shape marks optional may be omitted — never invent a
value you do not have; leave the field out instead):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "1.0",
  "kind": "codegen-mapping-manifest",
  "source": { "module": "shinro-migration/oms-camunda-application", "generatedAt": "<ISO-8601>", "generatorVersion": "shinro-agent" },
  "target": { "language": "go", "modulePath": "shinro-migration/oms-camunda-application", "projectRoot": "." },
  "mappings": [
    {
      "source": {
        "kind": "worker | bpmnElement | humanTask | decision | entryPoint",
        "workerId": "<the 'Worker id' line from workers/<jobType>.md — copy it verbatim>",
        "jobType": "<job type — for service-task workers>",
        "elementId": "<BPMN element id — for bpmn elements / human tasks>",
        "processId": "<owning process id>",
        "classificationKey": "<the classificationKey= shown on the element in processes/<id>.md; omit if none is shown>"
      },
      "target": {
        "construct": "activity | workflow | childWorkflow | signalHandler | timer | saga | comment",
        "family": "<same canonical vocabulary as construct>",
        "symbol": "<full Go symbol, e.g. shinro-migration/oms-camunda-application/activities.Charge>",
        "file": "<path relative to project root, e.g. activities/charge.go>",
        "startLine": 0
      },
      "decisions": {
        "sideEffectClass": "<from the worker md Classification>",
        "idempotencyKey": "<only if the worker md gives one>",
        "retryPolicy": "<copy the worker md 'Suggested retry policy' — e.g. {"maximumAttempts": 3, "nonRetryable": ["<BPMN code>"]}; OMIT this field entirely when the md gives no suggested policy — never hardcode a blanket default>",
        "coverageClass": "<AUTO | ASSISTED | MANUAL from Migration guidance>",
        "reviewRequired": false
      },
      "status": "generated"
    }
  ],
  "gaps": [
    { "source": { "kind": "...", "jobType": "...", "elementId": "...", "processId": "..." },
      "reason": "<why it could not be built>", "recommendation": "<what a human must do>", "severity": "blocker | warn" }
  ]
}
```

Rules:
- ONE mapping row per migrated element: every job worker, every human task
  (signal/update handler), every DMN decision, AND the workflow itself. Set the
  workflow's rows' `source.processId` and put the workflow function in
  `target.symbol`/`target.file` — the validator locates the workflow through them.
- `target.symbol` and `target.file` MUST be exact: the validator confirms the
  named function actually exists in that file. A wrong symbol/file is a hard error.
- `reviewRequired` MUST be true whenever the worker's coverage is ASSISTED or
  MANUAL, or its classification "requires human confirmation" — an auto-generated
  ASSISTED/MANUAL construct without the flag is a validator ERROR. Match
  `sideEffectClass` to the worker md exactly (a mismatch is an error), and give a
  non-idempotent activity an `idempotencyKey` or it is flagged.
- `retryPolicy` comes ONLY from the worker md's "Suggested retry policy" line (the
  analysis emits one for a minority of workers). OMIT it when the md gives none —
  never write a blanket `maximumAttempts: 3` for every row. It MUST be identical to
  the RetryPolicy you set in that activity's ActivityOptions in the generated code.
- Anything you leave as a TODO or mark a task `manual` goes in `gaps` (or as a
  mapping with `"status": "gap-needs-manual"`) — NEVER silently omit an element,
  or the validator reports it as a coverage gap.

Keep replies terse — your value is in the code and the task list.

## Completion
When every task in tasks.md is done or manual and the final build+vet pass is green, reply with exactly: MIGRATION_TASKS_COMPLETE (plus a short human-facing summary). Until then, always use a tool call or keep working — do not stop early.

Begin the Camunda → Temporal (Go) migration of `shinro-migration/oms-camunda-application`.

159|					return workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, shared.SignalSupportCorrection).HasReceive(ctx) || cancelSig != nil
160|				})
161|				if cancelSig != nil {
162|					// The interrupting subprocess wins; drop the stray
163|					// correction delivery.
164|					return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleCancel(cancelSig)
165|				}
166|				workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, shared.SignalSupportCorrection).Receive(ctx, &correction)

168|				// Re-enter Task_ValidateOrder (loop); the correction is
169|				// consumed and cleared by the next validation.
170|				continue
171|			}
172|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
173|		}
174|		order = validateOut.Order
175|		// The consumed correction is cleared (next validation passes nil —
176|		// parity of newCompleteCommand writing correctionItems=null).
177|		correctionItems = nil
178|
179|		// Task_UpdatePaymentPending: Dashboard: PAYMENT_PENDING
180|		if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
181|			shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusPaymentPending}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
182|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
183|		}
184|		if done, err := checkInterrupts(); done {
185|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
186|		}
187|
188|		// Catch_Payment: await Message_CapturePayment, racing the
189|		// interrupting Cancellation subprocess and the 30-day TTL timer.
190|		// (Also the landing point of the Bnd_InvalidPayment boundary below.)
191|		var capSig shared.CapturePaymentSignal
192|		workflow.Await(ctx, func() bool {
193|			return workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, shared.SignalCapturePayment).HasReceive(ctx) || cancelSig != nil || ttlFired
194|		})
195|		if cancelSig != nil {
196|			// Drop any stray payment delivery; the subprocess wins.
197|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleCancel(cancelSig)
198|		}
199|		if ttlFired {
200|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleTTL()
201|		}
202|		workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, shared.SignalCapturePayment).Receive(ctx, &capSig)
203|		payment = *capSig.Payment
204|
205|		// Task_ValidatePayment: Validate payment RRN — boundary
206|		// Bnd_InvalidPayment (error INVALID_PAYMENT) loops back to the
207|		// Catch_Payment wait; the next CapturePayment message overwrites
208|		// the stale payment.
209|		var payOut shared.ValidatePaymentOutput
210|		err = workflow.ExecuteActivity(workflow.WithActivityOptions(ctx, validatePayment),
211|			activities.ValidatePayment,
212|			shared.ValidatePaymentInput{Order: order, Payment: &payment}).Get(ctx, &payOut)

214|			if isBpmnError(err, shared.ErrInvalidPayment) {

216|				// Bnd_InvalidPayment → Flow_bnd_catchpay → Catch_Payment.
217|				if done, ierr := checkInterrupts(); done {
218|					return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, ierr
219|				}
220|				continue
221|			}
222|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
223|		}
224|		payment = *payOut.Payment
225|		break
226|	}
227|
228|	// Task_UpdateCaptured: Dashboard: PAYMENT_CAPTURED
229|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
230|		shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusPaymentCaptured}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
231|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
232|	}
233|	if done, err := checkInterrupts(); done {
234|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
235|	}
236|
237|	// Task_Enrich: Enrich with PIM
238|	var enrichOut shared.EnrichOrderOutput
239|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.EnrichOrder,
240|		shared.EnrichOrderInput{Order: order}).Get(ctx, &enrichOut); err != nil {
241|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
242|	}
243|	order = enrichOut.Order
244|
245|	// Task_Publish: Publish to fulfillment
246|	if _, err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.PublishFulfillment,
247|		shared.PublishFulfillmentInput{Order: order, Payment: &payment}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
248|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
249|	}
250|
251|	// Task_UpdateFulfilled: Dashboard: FULFILLED
252|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
253|		shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusFulfilled}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
254|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
255|	}
256|
257|	// EndEvent_Done: Order fulfilled
258|	return shared.OrderProcessingResult{
259|		OrderId: orderID,
260|		Outcome: "FULFILLED",
261|		Order:   order,
262|		Payment: &payment,
263|	}, nil
264|}

266|// isBpmnError reports whether err is an application error carrying the given
267|// BPMN error code (the Go equivalent of a Zeebe boundary error event matched
268|// on errorCode).
269|func isBpmnError(err error, code string) bool {
270|	ae, ok := err.(*temporal.ApplicationError)
271|	return ok && ae.Type() == code

15|// (CommerceWorkers#validateOrder).

18|// webhook order:
19|//
20|//  1. apply any pending SupportCorrection (delivered as the

22|//     parity of WorkflowState.ApplyCorrection in the original Temporal app;

26|//     drives the correction loop); on success complete with the validated
27|//     order and clear the consumed correctionItems variable.
28|//
29|// No external I/O — validation is idempotent and safe to re-run.
30|func ValidateOrder(ctx context.Context, in shared.ValidateOrderInput) (shared.ValidateOrderOutput, error) {
31|	logger := slog.Default().With("activity", "validate-order")
32|
33|	order := in.Order
34|	// Apply any pending SupportCorrection (delivered as correctionItems)
35|	// before re-validating — parity of WorkflowState.ApplyCorrection.
36|	order = applyCorrection(order, in.CorrectionItems)
37|

39|

41|		logger.WarnContext(ctx, "order validation failed", "rejection", rejection)
42|		// Non-retryable business failure -> correction loop (not an activity
43|		// retry). BPMN error INVALID_ORDER -> boundary event Bnd_InvalidOrder.
44|		return shared.ValidateOrderOutput{}, temporal.NewNonRetryableApplicationError(
45|			rejection, shared.ErrInvalidOrder, nil)
46|	}
47|

49|	// Echo the (validated) order back; the consumed correction is cleared by
50|	// the workflow (correctionItems is nilled on re-entry).
51|	return shared.ValidateOrderOutput{Order: order}, nil

14|// ValidatePayment reimplements Camunda job worker "validate-payment"
15|// (OmsWorkers#validatePayment).
16|//
17|// Business failures (bad RRN, wrong amount) raise the BPMN error
18|// INVALID_PAYMENT, caught by the boundary event that loops back to the
19|// CapturePayment wait — the parity of the original Temporal payment retry
20|// loop that awaited a fresh CapturePayment signal. Transient/system
21|// failures return plain (retryable) errors and are retried up to the
22|// task's configured retry count (5).
23|func ValidatePayment(ctx context.Context, in shared.ValidatePaymentInput) (shared.ValidatePaymentOutput, error) {
24|	logger := slog.Default().With("activity", "validate-payment")
25|	payment := in.Payment
26|	expectedAmount := in.Order.TotalAmountOrZero()
27|
28|	logger.InfoContext(ctx, "validate-payment started", "rrn", rrnString(payment))
29|
30|	if rejection := paymentValidationError(payment, expectedAmount); rejection != "" {
31|		logger.WarnContext(ctx, "payment validation failed", "rejection", rejection)
32|		// BPMN error -> boundary event loops back to the CapturePayment wait.
33|		// No need to clear the payment variable: the next CapturePayment
34|		// message overwrites it (mirrors the Temporal loop awaiting a fresh
35|		// signal).
36|		return shared.ValidatePaymentOutput{}, temporal.NewNonRetryableApplicationError(
37|			rejection, shared.ErrInvalidPayment, nil)
38|	}
39|
40|	logger.InfoContext(ctx, "validate-payment completed", "rrn", payment.Rrn)
41|	// Complete with the payment variable (echoed unchanged).
42|	return shared.ValidatePaymentOutput{Payment: payment}, nil
43|}
44|
45|// paymentValidationError returns "" when the payment is valid, else the
46|// rejection reason (OmsWorkers#validationError, same messages).
47|func paymentValidationError(payment *shared.PaymentInput, expectedAmount float64) string {
48|	if payment == nil || payment.Rrn == "" {
49|		return "payment RRN is empty"
50|	}
51|	if len(payment.Rrn) != 12 {
52|		return fmt.Sprintf("invalid RRN length %d; must be 12 digits", len(payment.Rrn))
53|	}
54|	for i := 0; i < len(payment.Rrn); i++ {
55|		c := payment.Rrn[i]
56|		if c < '0' || c > '9' {
57|			return "RRN must contain only digits"
58|		}
59|	}
60|	if payment.Amount <= 0 {
61|		return fmt.Sprintf("invalid payment amount: %v", payment.Amount)
62|	}
63|	// Compare money as integer cents; exact float equality is unsafe for
64|	// amounts that aren't representable in binary floating point.
65|	if math.Round(payment.Amount*100) != math.Round(expectedAmount*100) {
66|		return fmt.Sprintf("payment amount %.2f does not match order total %.2f", payment.Amount, expectedAmount)
67|	}
68|	return ""
69|}

71|func rrnString(p *shared.PaymentInput) string {
72|	if p == nil {
73|		return ""
74|	}
75|	return p.Rrn

26|// over the orders_dashboard table) that is not portable to this Go module
27|// without a driver/DSN, so the default implementation fails loudly instead
28|// of pretending the projection was written. Wire a real implementation
29|// (e.g. database/sql + the same UPDATE/INSERT upsert SQL) in cmd/worker.

20|// terminal state was applied, and the workflow instance ends — parity of
21|// the Zeebe terminate event aborting the whole instance.
22|func ErrTerminated(outcome string) error {
23|	return temporal.NewNonRetryableApplicationError("order-processing terminated: "+outcome, "TERMINATED", nil)
24|}

26|// OrderProcessingWorkflow reimplements Camunda process "order-processing"
27|// (models/order-processing.bpmn) as a Temporal workflow.
28|//
29|// BPMN → Temporal mapping:
30|//
31|//   - service tasks (update-dashboard / validate-order / validate-payment /
32|//     enrich-order / publish-fulfillment) → activities; retry policies come
33|//     from the BPMN task "retries" attributes (validate-payment=5, all other
34|//     service tasks 2147483647 ≈ unbounded → SDK default policy, no cap);
35|//   - message catch events (Catch_Payment, Catch_Correction) → signal
36|//     channels on the same message names, correlated by workflow id
37|//     (parity of the zeebe correlationKey=orderId — the workflow id is
38|//     derived from the order id by the starter);
39|//   - boundary error events → typed non-retryable application errors:
40|//     Bnd_InvalidOrder (code INVALID_ORDER) on Task_ValidateOrder drives
41|//     the correction loop; Bnd_InvalidPayment (code INVALID_PAYMENT) on
42|//     Task_ValidatePayment loops back to the Catch_Payment wait;
43|//   - interrupting message event subprocess "Cancellation"
44|//     (Message_CancelOrder → Dashboard CANCELLED → terminate) and
45|//     interrupting timer event subprocess "Order TTL (30 days)"
46|//     (PT720H → Dashboard EXPIRED → terminate) → one workflow.Go goroutine
47|//     per trigger buffers the signal / timer into a shared pointer; the
48|//     main flow checks both at every catch point and after every activity,
49|//     and the first armed trigger wins (cancel before TTL, matching the
50|//     interrupting subprocesses' shared process-level scope). An interrupt
51|//     applies its dashboard step then ends the workflow with the TERMINATED
52|//     error (terminate end event).
53|func OrderProcessingWorkflow(ctx workflow.Context, in shared.OrderProcessingInput) (shared.OrderProcessingResult, error) {
54|	logger := workflow.GetLogger(ctx)
55|
56|	// Base activity options: a generous start-to-close bound. The
57|	// "unbounded" service tasks keep the SDK default retry policy (no
58|	// MaximumAttempts cap — parity of retries="2147483647"); validate-payment
59|	// gets MaximumAttempts: 5 (parity of retries="5").
60|	base := workflow.ActivityOptions{StartToCloseTimeout: 5 * time.Minute}
61|	validatePayment := base
62|	validatePayment.RetryPolicy = &temporal.RetryPolicy{MaximumAttempts: 5}
63|	ctx = workflow.WithActivityOptions(ctx, base)
64|
65|	orderID := in.OrderId
66|	order := in.Order
67|
68|	// --- interrupting subprocess "Cancellation" (Message_CancelOrder) ---
69|	cancelSig := (*shared.CancelOrderSignal)(nil)
70|	workflow.Go(ctx, func(gctx workflow.Context) {
71|		var sig shared.CancelOrderSignal
72|		workflow.GetSignalChannel(gctx, shared.SignalCancelOrder).Receive(gctx, &sig)
73|		s := sig
74|		cancelSig = &s
75|	})
76|
77|	// --- interrupting timer subprocess "Order TTL (30 days)" (PT720H) ---
78|	// workflow.NewTimer is deterministic; the future completes 720h after
79|	// the start event on every replay.
80|	ttlFired := false
81|	workflow.Go(ctx, func(gctx workflow.Context) {
82|		if err := workflow.NewTimer(gctx, orderTTL).Get(gctx, nil); err != nil {
83|			return
84|		}
85|		ttlFired = true
86|	})
87|
88|	// handleTTL runs the TTL subprocess body: Dashboard EXPIRED, then the
89|	// terminate end event (End_Expired).
90|	handleTTL := func() error {
91|		logger.Info("order TTL (30 days) elapsed")
92|		if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
93|			shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusExpired}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
94|			return err
95|		}
96|		// End_Expired: terminate end event.
97|		return ErrTerminated("EXPIRED")
98|	}
99|
100|	// handleCancel runs the Cancellation subprocess body: Dashboard
101|	// CANCELLED, then the terminate end event (End_Cancelled).
102|	handleCancel := func(sig *shared.CancelOrderSignal) error {
103|		logger.Info("cancel order signal received reason=", sig.Reason)
104|		if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
105|			shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusCancelled}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
106|			return err
107|		}
108|		// End_Cancelled: terminate end event.
109|		return ErrTerminated("CANCELLED")
110|	}
111|
112|	// checkInterrupts handles interrupts that arrived while the main flow
113|	// was inside an activity. The cancel signal wins the race, matching the
114|	// interrupting subprocesses' shared process-level scope.
115|	checkInterrupts := func() (bool, error) {
116|		if cancelSig != nil {
117|			return true, handleCancel(cancelSig)
118|		}
119|		if ttlFired {
120|			return true, handleTTL()
121|		}
122|		return false, nil
123|	}
124|
125|	payment := shared.PaymentInput{} // zero value until CapturePayment arrives
126|	var correctionItems []shared.OrderItem // pending SupportCorrection, cleared once consumed
127|
128|	// Task_UpdateReceived: Dashboard: ORDER_RECEIVED
129|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
130|		shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusOrderReceived}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
131|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
132|	}
133|	if done, err := checkInterrupts(); done {
134|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
135|	}
136|
137|	for {
138|		// Task_ValidateOrder: Validate order (Commerce API). The activity
139|		// applies correctionItems itself (parity of applyCorrection) and
140|		// throws BPMN error INVALID_ORDER on business failure.
141|		var validateOut shared.ValidateOrderOutput
142|		err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.ValidateOrder,
143|			shared.ValidateOrderInput{Order: order, CorrectionItems: correctionItems}).Get(ctx, &validateOut)

164|					if correctionCh.Receive(ctx, &correction) {
165|						return true
166|					}
167|					return cancelSig != nil
168|				})
169|				if cancelSig != nil {
170|					// The interrupting subprocess wins; drop the stray
171|					// correction delivery.
172|					return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleCancel(cancelSig)
173|				}
174|				correctionItems = correction.Items
175|				// Re-enter Task_ValidateOrder (loop); the correction is
176|				// consumed and cleared by the next validation.
177|				continue
178|			}
179|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
180|		}
181|		order = validateOut.Order
182|		// The consumed correction is cleared (next validation passes nil —
183|		// parity of newCompleteCommand writing correctionItems=null).
184|		correctionItems = nil
185|
186|		// Task_UpdatePaymentPending: Dashboard: PAYMENT_PENDING

188|			shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusPaymentPending}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
189|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
190|		}
191|		if done, err := checkInterrupts(); done {
192|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
193|		}
194|
195|		// Catch_Payment: await Message_CapturePayment, racing the
196|		// interrupting Cancellation subprocess and the 30-day TTL timer.
197|		// (Also the landing point of the Bnd_InvalidPayment boundary below.)
198|		capCh := workflow.GetSignalChannel(ctx, shared.SignalCapturePayment)
199|		var capSig shared.CapturePaymentSignal
200|		workflow.Await(ctx, func() bool {
201|			if capCh.Receive(ctx, &capSig) {
202|				return true
203|			}
204|			return cancelSig != nil || ttlFired
205|		})
206|		if cancelSig != nil {
207|			// Drop any stray payment delivery; the subprocess wins.
208|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleCancel(cancelSig)
209|		}
210|		if ttlFired {
211|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, handleTTL()
212|		}

217|			capSig.Payment = &shared.PaymentInput{}

221|		// Task_ValidatePayment: Validate payment RRN — boundary

226|		err = workflow.ExecuteActivity(workflow.WithActivityOptions(ctx, validatePayment),

228|			shared.ValidatePaymentInput{Order: order, Payment: &payment}).Get(ctx, &payOut)

234|					return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, ierr
235|				}
236|				continue
237|			}
238|			return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
239|		}
240|		payment = *payOut.Payment
241|		break
242|	}
243|
244|	// Task_UpdateCaptured: Dashboard: PAYMENT_CAPTURED
245|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
246|		shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusPaymentCaptured}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
247|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
248|	}
249|	if done, err := checkInterrupts(); done {
250|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
251|	}
252|
253|	// Task_Enrich: Enrich with PIM
254|	var enrichOut shared.EnrichOrderOutput
255|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.EnrichOrder,
256|		shared.EnrichOrderInput{Order: order}).Get(ctx, &enrichOut); err != nil {

258|	}
259|	order = enrichOut.Order
260|
261|	// Task_Publish: Publish to fulfillment
262|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.PublishFulfillment,
263|		shared.PublishFulfillmentInput{Order: order, Payment: &payment}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
264|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
265|	}
266|
267|	// Task_UpdateFulfilled: Dashboard: FULFILLED
268|	if err := workflow.ExecuteActivity(ctx, activities.UpdateDashboard,
269|		shared.UpdateDashboardInput{OrderId: orderID, Status: shared.StatusFulfilled}).Get(ctx, nil); err != nil {
270|		return shared.OrderProcessingResult{}, err
271|	}
272|
273|	// EndEvent_Done: Order fulfilled
274|	return shared.OrderProcessingResult{
275|		OrderId: orderID,
276|		Outcome: "FULFILLED",
277|		Order:   order,
278|		Payment: &payment,
279|	}, nil
280|}

282|// isBpmnError reports whether err is an application error carrying the given
283|// BPMN error code (the Go equivalent of a Zeebe boundary error event matched
284|// on errorCode).
285|func isBpmnError(err error, code string) bool {
286|	ae, ok := err.(*temporal.ApplicationError)
287|	return ok && ae.Type() == code

59|// (ValidationFailure parity), and we return a plain (retryable) error for it.

67|		return shared.UpdateDashboardOutput{}, fmt.Errorf("unsupported dashboard status: %s", in.Status)
68|	}

16|type FulfillmentPublisher interface {

18|	// to re-run: msg.EventId ("fulfillment:<orderId>:v1") is the idempotency
19|	// key — the downstream consumer must dedupe on it for retries to be safe.
20|	Publish(ctx context.Context, msg *shared.FulfillmentMessage) error

24|// worker's mocked publish: it constructs the wire message and logs it. It is
25|// NOT a broker client — wire a real Kafka/Pub-Sub publisher here (keeping the
26|// EventId as the dedup key) for production traffic.

33|		"eventId", msg.EventId,
34|		"orderId", msg.OrderId,
35|		"customerId", msg.CustomerId,
36|		"itemCount", len(msg.Items),

39|	return nil

57|// schemaVersion 1, payment details, enriched items) and publishes it.
58|// Idempotent: the event id is derived from the order id, so retries
59|// publish the same logical event.

Now I understand the root cause. The TTL test passes because its 1h timer fires *before* the 10s test deadline. But in the cancel test, `orderTTL` is still 720h: the mock clock's "auto fire timer" for the 720h timer fires at exactly the test deadline, and the deadline-exceeded wins before the workflow can re-evaluate its Await. The fix: shorten `orderTTL` in the cancel test too, so the timer fires before the deadline and the cancel-vs-TTL race is actually exercised.
